audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0, 2 and 3 disagreed with both the packet chart (Skill, Skill, Neeko, Skill, Neeko, Ornn, Ornn) and the page's own whys.
audit.why: whys[2] reads 'she edges this window' while the chart rendered Ornn; whys[3] reads 'Coinflip' while the chart rendered Ornn; row 0 was handed to Neeko when the packet calls it Skill. The already-audited mirror flipped exactly these three rows to Skill / Neeko / Skill.
audit.corrected: Row 0 Neeko -> Skill (5/10), row 2 Ornn -> Neeko (4/10), row 3 Ornn -> Skill (5/10), in BOTH layers as one group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was described as 'her R' with no range, cooldown, or the mechanic that actually makes it dangerous.
audit.why: Pop Blossom is 600 range on 120/105/90s, knocks up on the leap and stuns on landing — and Riot's text ends with 'The preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised.' The hidden wind-up, not the damage, is why level 6 is her row.
audit.corrected: Spike text now names Pop Blossom with 600/120s and states that the wind-up is invisible while she is disguised, which is the cue to hold W rather than spend it on poke.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: none of Neeko's five abilities were named. Two decisive interactions were absent entirely.
audit.why: (1) Inherent Glamour's text: 'Receiving immobilizing crowd control ... breaks the disguise.' Searing Charge's terrain knockup and Call of the Forge God's knockup are immobilizing CC, so Ornn is one of the few top laners who strips a disguised Neeko on contact — that never reached the page. (2) Tangle-Barbs: 'If the tangle kills an enemy or passes through a champion, it becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer.' Standing behind an ally or a dying minion is what turns a dodgeable 1000-range root into an unavoidable long one. Also missing: Blooming Burst is 800 range on 9s and 'blooms again on hitting champions', Shapesplitter's clone is on 16s at rank 1, and its passive adds bonus damage every third attack.
audit.corrected: All five named with ranges and cooldowns; the disguise-break and the Tangle-Barbs upgrade condition now appear in the TL;DR, the dos, the trade lines and report[5].
sources: kit: Ornn E and R knockup flags

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried 'Her root — extends through targets' with no numbers and a placeholder committal-tool line.
audit.why: Tangle-Barbs' 12s at rank 1 is the window Ornn's whole pattern keys off, and Blooming Burst at 9s is short enough that waiting it out is not a plan.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block now gives Tangle-Barbs 1000/12s and its upgrade condition, Blooming Burst 9s and Pop Blossom 120s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were verbatim copies of tradeGood/tradeBad, and the page used male pronouns for Neeko throughout.
audit.why: Three of six lane rules said the same sentence, and 'brittle-proc him' reads as untouched template text.
audit.corrected: Each rule now carries a distinct mechanic; pronouns fixed in every string edited.

notes: Best find here: Inherent Glamour breaks on 'receiving immobilizing crowd control', and Ornn's E and R are both knockups — so he strips a disguised Neeko on contact. That interaction was nowhere on the page and is now in three places. DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: whether Volcanic Rupture's grounding can deny Pop Blossom's leap (the leap is flagged dash and Q is flagged grounding, but neither appears in Riot's description of Volcanic Rupture, so I did not tell the player it works), whether a slow counts as immobilizing for the disguise break (it does not say), and whether Tangle-Barbs upgrades through a clone. SAMPLE-SIZE NOTE FOR THE USER: the mirror's audit recorded packet.games of only 21 on its side while this brief reports 829 — worth confirming which figure the site renders. I did not touch diff, tone, diffRating or carryRating: at 52.71% this reads closer to EVEN than FAV, but the mirror already moved its own ratings and I did not want to introduce a fight over them.
